#219 correctness review, round 1: BLOCK

Exact head: `0a693ca73abf7a81cb3cd3f6f63d70978ddd3e83`.

**F001: Rust and Copilot keep the old boot credential throughout the restart wait.** The daemon deliberately generates and publishes a new bearer key on every successful boot (`crates/daemon/src/auth.rs:1-20,121-144`; `daemon/src/lib.rs:919-930,1121-1124`). A call starting during the closed-port interval can still read the previous boot's published key.

The Rust client reads that key only at construction (`crates/cli/src/client.rs:163-170`), authenticates the builder once before its retry loop and clones that already-authenticated request for every attempt (`:564-594`). Copilot likewise calls `readKey()` once, constructs the Authorization header, then passes that unchanged init through every refused-connection retry (`.copilot/extensions/pij/store.mjs:564-582,586-616`). Neither path refreshes credentials within this recovery.

Thus a real bounce can produce refused connections followed by a healthy new daemon rejecting the stale credential with 401. The command still fails, now with an authentication error, rather than surviving the restart. This directly affects the native directory/requests calls and Copilot sends the PR intends to repair. OMP's existing key-refresh path and the router's repeated probes do not repair the Rust or Copilot paths.

Fix: preserve the distinction between local boot credentials and explicit job tokens, and refresh the former safely as part of connection-refusal recovery. Keep the no-replay rule for requests that could have reached an application handler. Add a recovery test that actually changes the published boot credential and makes the replacement server validate Authorization; cover both Rust and Copilot. The present recovery fixtures keep the same key and accept the request without validating a rotated credential, so they cannot detect this failure.

The retry classification itself is appropriately narrow: Rust checks the underlying ConnectionRefused kind; JS checks refusal codes; response-body failures and resets do not re-enter these new loops. The nine-attempt default schedule, zero-wait override for native CLI/router, Rust fast-path exclusions, and extension route allowlists are present. Registration, inbox, activity and turn-end calls retain their own/immediate behavior rather than inheriting the new tool wait.

**Evidence:** `just pr-freeze 219` returned FINAL at this head; detached tree clean. [CI run 42764036542](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42764036542) records the exact head. Its successful Rust job's [JUnit artifact 13739600549](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42764036542/artifacts/13739600549) contains 2,416 executed tests, zero failures/errors; nextest reports six additional skips. The recovery, bounded-down, request-read-once and environment-parser cases ran and passed. Node 22 passed the 70-test router and 23-test daemon-http suites; its native suite passed 350 cases, including all three new F174 tests. These do not exercise real per-boot key rotation.

Cost inspection: no new process launch or periodic activity; waits occur after explicit safe connection refusals, with the extension loops excluded. Source trace, not a reviewer-run live bounce. No real credentials were read, and no local builds/tests, daemon restart, settings changes, lifecycle mutations or product edits were performed.
